newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Shell said among oil firms eyeing Russia's SIDANKO.
newsitem.headline: Shell said among oil firms eyeing Russia's SIDANKO.

text.p: Russia's prominent Uneximbank said on Wednesday it was in talks with foreign oil firms, including the Royal Dutch/Shell group, on the sale of a 34 percent stake in Russian oil group SIDANKO.

"Shell is one of a number of companies we are talking to on the sale of the 34 percent stake (in SIDANKO) held in the Cyprus offshore holding company," Modest Kolerov, deputy head of Uneximbank's information department, told Reuters.
He said the shares would probably be sold this year.
Uneximbank, through its affiliate, Interros-Oil, owns the 34 percent stake and used it as collateral when it got a loan from a Cyprus-registered unknown, Kantupun Holding Company.

"The overall value of this collateral was around $300 million," Kolerov said, adding Uneximbank, one of Russia's most powerful commercial banks, had raised around $700 million for SIDANKO, Russia's fourth-largest crude oil producer.

A senior Uneximbank source said late last month the bank was considering selling the stake to attract investment in the oil firm but said the bank would hold on to a controlling 51 percent stake in SIDANKO.
Vertically-integrated SIDANKO produced 20.81 million tonnes (416,000 barrels per day) of oil and gas condensate in 1996, down from 22.87 million (457,000 bpd) in 1995.
SIDANKO production units include Kondpetroleum COND.RTS, Varyoganneftegaz VJGZ.RTS and Chernogorneft CHGZ.RTS.
